mechanism_narrative: The observed four-week trend of increasing RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -10.0% to -5.9%, indicates a sustained recovery in consumer activity that will continue to drive retail and recreation visits higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, indicated by the recent rise from -13.6% to -2.3%, suggests a return to office work that will boost weekday retail and recreation activity, especially if WORKPLACES crosses -2% in the next week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -2% in the next week
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises above -2% but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks compared to the current level, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent increase in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility over the last two weeks suggests a synergistic effect of increased commuting, which will directly translate to higher foot traffic in retail and recreation areas, especially during peak hours.
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue their upward trend, but RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility from 7.6% to 5.3% over the last three weeks indicates people are spending less time at home, a behavioral shift that will free up time for out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, provided there are no new restrictions.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to decline but RETAIL_REC also declines over the next four weeks, or if new public health restrictions are imposed, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The steady increase in PARKS mobility from -23.6% to -15.7% over the last four weeks suggests a broader trend of increased outdoor activity and comfort with public spaces, which typically precedes or accompanies a rise in general retail and recreation visits.
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility continues its upward trend but RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The high and relatively stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility (around +40%) indicates essential activity is robust. As non-essential RETAIL_REC mobility is still negative but improving, the gap between essential and non-essential spending will narrow, driving RETAIL_REC upwards.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM drops below +35% or RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks despite stable GROCERY_PHARM, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: While TRANSIT has recently increased, the dip at t-2w (-10.4%) followed by a rebound suggests volatility. If TRANSIT mobility fails to sustain its recent upward momentum and drops below -5% in the next week, it will signal a broader hesitation in public movement, negatively impacting RETAIL_REC in the short term.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -5% in the next week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls below -5% but RETAIL_REC increases in the subsequent week, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: The inverse relationship between WORKPLACES (trending up from t-2w) and RESIDENTIAL (trending down) indicates a shift from home-based activities to work-related commuting. This fundamental shift in daily routines will inherently lead to more opportunities for retail and recreation visits outside the home.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues to rise while RESIDENTIAL falls, but RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks, this hypothesis is falsified.
